name: Aarhus University
about: Aarhus University reports about 37,500 students in its 2025 statistics. Its English bachelor's list covers computing, business and cognitive science: five subjects and six campus offerings, with Economics and Business Administration in both Aarhus and Herning. For 2027, Cognitive Science may switch to Danish; AU expects an update around December 2026, so confirm its language before planning an application. The university's other campuses and research locations do not host the English offerings listed here.

languageOfInstruction.note: A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

ibEquivalences.subject: Social Studies
ibEquivalences.note: AU's own addition to the Agency's table: "Global Politics HL: Recognised as Social Science B"; "Global Politics SL: Recognised as Social Science B in combination with Economics SL/HL". Page revised 21.08.2026, read 25 Sep 2026.

levelRaise.text: AU accepts supplementary courses, and counts College Board AP and British A-level courses as A level.
levelRaise.multiple: AU accepts as many as you need passed before 5 July, and at most two passed after it.

groups.unknownAfterResults: Whether AU's conditional admission after 5 July is open to applicants from outside the EU/EEA is not recorded — ask AU; otherwise every course has to be passed by 5 July, before your IB results.

levelRaise.timing: Pass it by 5 July, or after 5 July as conditional admission with documentation by 5 September (at most two after 5 July).
levelRaise.quota2Question: Whether AU's conditional admission after 5 July applies to quota 2 applicants, whose documents are due by 15 March, is not recorded — ask AU.

admissionRoutes.short: an assessment of your subject grades and experience
admissionRoutes.text: AU assesses the average of your grades in the programme's quota 2 subjects, and can add to it for documented relevant experience (work, internships, a folk high school; 4–12 months). Everything must be documented by 15 March.

notes: Cognitive Science is currently taught in English, but AU anticipates a switch to Danish for autumn 2027. If implemented, Danish A and English B would be required. Check the programme page after 1 December 2026 before relying on an English-only pathway.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

AU publishes a quota 1 qualifying-examination GPA floor of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale for all six currently English-taught campus paths. For Economics and Business Administration in Herning, the Danish programme page states the floor while the English page omits it. Below the floor, applicants must use quota 2; this is not a universal IB minimum or a quota 2 floor. Cognitive Science's 2027 teaching language remains unconfirmed.
Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development add a second floor: a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A specifically, on top of the overall 6.0.
The 6.0 floor is not the cut-off. The cut-off is what the last admitted applicant actually scored, and in 2026 that was 11.4 for Computer Science and 11.2 for Data Science.

AU tells "Danish applicants" (on its Data Science page, "applicants with Danish A") to treat the English-taught Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development degrees as the harder route and to apply to the Danish-taught equivalents (Datalogi, Datavidenskab, It-produktudvikling) as well. For Data Science AU says outright that the English version "is intended for international students". The two versions lead to the same English-taught master's.

The standby cut-off is published next to the quota 1 cut-off and is usually lower — dramatically so for IT Product Development in 2026 (10.1 in quota 1, 6.9 for standby). You have to tick standby when you apply, and the standby application deadline is 5 July.

Herning is not Aarhus. AU Herning is a small campus roughly an hour west of Aarhus in a town of about 50,000, running a few business, engineering and technology programmes. Its Economics and Business Administration degree is academically similar to the Aarhus one but had a 2026 cut-off of 6.9 against 9.2.

Paying applicants cannot apply in the year they earn the IB: their final diploma and transcripts are due 15 March at noon. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants must establish their actual tuition/residence exemption status; a Danish address alone is not a published tuition exemption.

For applications after 1 November 2026, the EUR 150 application fee is non-refundable even on enrolment, and the whole first year of tuition is paid before the first semester. The published tuition schedule is still 2026/27; 2027/28 rates are not yet published.

AU’s Course Results page still mentions GSK, while the national recognition authority distinguishes qualification supplementation through HF-enkeltfag from GSK subject-level supplementation. Follow the national qualification rule and confirm the individual route with AU.

The English first-year offerings listed here are in Aarhus and Herning. AU also has Emdrup (Copenhagen), Viborg/Foulum, Roskilde and Flakkebjerg locations; these are not additional campuses for the listed English degrees.
